lead: A skill tells the agent how to work. Open a card for when to use it and how it runs.

items.name: Work Desk
items.invoke: Paste a transcript, drop a file in inbox, or ask for the daily list.
items.summary: Turns messy talks into the morning board.
items.when: Transcripts, inbox files, Today, user groups, research, strategy, access, library, language, patterns, skills, branding, prototype, or Figma.
how: Fold the talk into that team's board.
Write board copy with Shaun writing.
Fold product words with UX writing.
Fold recipes with UX Patterns. Wait for Yes.
Fold studies with UX Research. Wait for Build plan.
Fold Figma library work with Figma. Live Astral first.
Move processed inbox files to archive.
items.note: Do not invent groups, insights, or next steps a talk has not named. Never store a password.

items.name: UX writing
items.invoke: /ux-writing
items.summary: Writes Astral UI copy with ORCA+ context.
items.when: Labels, buttons, errors, empty states, onboarding, tooltips, help, notifications, permissions, or modals.
how: Name the object, relationship, CTA, and attributes first.
Add role, intent, state, surface, locale, and risk.
en-GB-oxendict. Sentence case. Card subtext starts with a capital. Action-led CTAs.
The glossary outranks generic language guidance.
items.note: Do not invent product behaviour. Language entries stay the glossary.

items.name: UX Patterns
items.invoke: /ux-patterns
items.summary: Inspects the product, then recommends one change.
items.when: A flow, filter, create, select, overflow, scrollbar, library drift, or pattern check.
how: Run the library check when the job is drift or a duplicate control.
Stop until you say Yes. Then prototype and record it.
items.note: Read-only until Yes. Product memory sits in docs/ux/. Native overflow lives in references/scrollbars.md.

items.name: UX Research
items.invoke: /ux-research
items.summary: Reviews what we already know before it plans a study.
items.when: What we know, what needs testing, build a study, analyse sessions, or update journeys and KEIs.
how: Wait for Build plan before branded research files.
items.note: Never invent quotes, scores, or personas. Study memory sits in docs/research/.

items.name: Figma
items.invoke: /figma
items.summary: Keeps the IMSERV Design System file in step with live Astral.
items.when: Update Figma from the library or prototype, construct a component, or bind variables.
how: Inventory live Astral and the Figma file.
Map tokens and variants with the name table.
Construct one unmatched component from the construction notes.
Screenshot against live CSS. Check icon size, type size, font, placeholder copy, and placeholder icons. Ask them to Publish.
items.note: Coded library and prototype are the source of truth. Map, transform, then construct. Do not invent a CI or Storybook sync.

items.name: Shaun writing
items.invoke: Ask to write, rewrite, or review copy in Shaun's voice.
items.summary: Recognise, Shape, Reframe. Clear, human, useful.
items.when: Interface text, case studies, articles, or a tone check.
how: Recognise what the text is trying to do.
Shape it so the point is easy to hold.
Reframe so it sounds like a careful thought, not a generator.
items.note: Work Desk copy follows this skill. No colons, semicolons, or em dashes in board text.

items.name: Create skill
items.invoke: Ask to author a new skill or how SKILL.md is structured.
items.summary: Writes a Cursor Agent Skill.
items.when: A new skill, or questions about SKILL.md.
how: Ask purpose, where it lives, and when it should run.
Keep verbatim wording the user asked to keep.

items.name: Create rule
items.invoke: Ask for a project rule, AGENTS.md, or .cursor/rules.
items.summary: Writes persistent agent guidance.
items.when: Coding standards, folder rules, or always-on instructions.
how: Choose a rule file in .cursor/rules or AGENTS.md.

items.name: Create hook
items.invoke: Ask for a Cursor hook or hooks.json.
items.summary: Adds scripts around agent events.
items.when: Hooks, hooks.json, or automation around agent runs.
how: Register it so it runs on the named event.

items.name: Create subagent
items.invoke: /create-subagent or ask for a custom subagent.
items.summary: Makes a specialised agent with its own prompt.
items.when: A reviewer, debugger, or domain helper that should run apart.
how: Keep it isolated from the parent chat.

items.name: Canvas
items.invoke: A durable visual beside the chat. Tables, charts, audits.
items.summary: Opens a live React canvas next to the chat.
items.when: Analytics, investigations, or any result that needs layout rather than a dump.
how: Prefer it over a markdown table when the data is the deliverable.
items.note: Use Visualize for a small chart in the transcript.

items.name: Visualize
items.invoke: /visualize
items.summary: Draws a compact chart or diagram in the chat.
items.when: A small visual in the transcript.
how: Pick a table, Mermaid, or inline HTML.
items.note: Use Canvas when they will come back to it.

items.name: Loop
items.invoke: /loop 5m /foo
items.summary: Repeats a prompt or skill on an interval.
items.when: A recurring check in this session.

items.name: Automate
items.invoke: Ask to create a Cursor Automation.
items.summary: Sets up a scheduled Cursor agent.
items.when: Create a Cursor Automation, not generic CI.
how: Only start when they mean Cursor Automations.
Open the Automations editor with a draft.
items.note: Do not treat every automate request as this skill.

items.name: Autopilot
items.invoke: Ask to keep a PR merge-ready.
items.summary: Triages comments, resolves clear conflicts, and watches CI.
items.when: A pull request that should stay ready to merge.
how: Loop on CI until it is green or blocked.

items.name: Review
items.invoke: /review
items.summary: Asks whether to run Bugbot or Security Review.
items.when: You want a review and have not named which one.

items.name: Bugbot review
items.invoke: Ask for a Bugbot-like review of local changes.
items.summary: Reviews the diff for bugs.
items.when: You explicitly ask for Bugbot.
how: It reads the repo and the diff.
items.note: Do not run this unless asked.

items.name: Security review
items.invoke: Ask for a security review of local changes.
items.summary: Reviews the diff for security issues.
items.when: You explicitly ask for a security review.
how: It reads the repo and the diff.
items.note: Do not run this unless asked.

items.name: Split to PRs
items.invoke: Ask to split work into small pull requests.
items.summary: Breaks the current work into reviewable PRs.
items.when: A chat, a set of changes, a branch, or a PR should be split.

items.name: New repo
items.invoke: Ask to create a Cursor-hosted repo.
items.summary: Creates a project on Cursor and pushes it.
items.when: No git remote yet, or you ask to host on Cursor.
how: Install and sign in the origin CLI if needed.

items.name: Origin
items.invoke: origin.cursor.com auth, clone, or push failure.
items.summary: Installs and repairs the origin CLI.
items.when: The CLI is missing, outdated, or auth fails against origin.cursor.com.

items.name: Share
items.invoke: Ask to save, back up, or share this project on Cursor.
items.summary: Makes a saved copy on Cursor that is not public.
items.when: Save, back up, publish, or how not to lose the project.
how: Create a Cursor repo even if git was never used.

items.name: Cursor SDK
items.invoke: Ask about @cursor/sdk, Agent.create, or running agents from a script.
items.summary: Guides apps and CI that call Cursor agents.
items.when: TypeScript or Python SDK, pipelines, or /v1/agents.
how: Read the SDK skill first. The surface changes.
Wire MCP and streaming as the package documents.

items.name: Update Cursor settings
items.invoke: Ask to change editor settings in settings.json.
items.summary: Edits Cursor or VS Code user settings.
items.when: Theme, font, format on save, keybindings, or settings.json.

items.name: Update CLI config
items.invoke: Ask to change Cursor CLI config.
items.summary: Edits ~/.cursor/cli-config.json.
items.when: CLI permissions, approval mode, vim, sandbox, or display.

items.name: Status line
items.invoke: Ask for a custom CLI status line.
items.summary: Configures the CLI prompt footer.
items.when: statusline, CLI status bar, or session context above the prompt.

items.name: Goal
items.invoke: /goal
items.summary: Sets a goal Cursor will pursue to completion.
items.when: You name an objective to finish.
how: Work it with tools until it is done.

items.name: Onboard
items.invoke: /onboard
items.summary: A short Cursor onboarding interview.
items.when: You want Cursor to learn basics and pick a first goal.
how: Hand off. Do not execute setup in that run.

items.name: Shell
items.invoke: /shell
items.summary: Runs the rest of the line as a shell command.
items.when: You want the following text executed in the terminal.
how: Treat the rest of the request as a literal command.

items.name: Rename chat
items.invoke: /rename-chat
items.summary: Renames the current chat to match its focus.
items.when: You invoke /rename-chat. Optional text steers the title.

items.name: Deploy with Vercel
items.invoke: /deploy-with-vercel or ask to deploy on Vercel.
items.summary: Links the repo and deploys with Vercel MCP.
items.when: You want this repository on Vercel.

items.name: Migrate to skills
items.invoke: Ask to convert rules or slash commands into skills.
items.summary: Turns .mdc rules and commands into SKILL.md files.
items.when: Migrate Applied intelligently rules or .cursor/commands.
